chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no servant but that there is wisdom in his head and an Angel withholds it. So when he is arrogant, (the Angel) says to him: 'Be humble, may Allah drop you!' So he does not cease to be the greatest of the people within himself and the smallest of the people in the eyes of the people. And when he is humble, Allah, Might and Majestic, raises him, then (the Angel) says to him: 'Be dignified, may Allah dignify you!' So he does not cease to be the smallest of the people within himself and the highest of the people in the eyes of the people.

key_terms.أَصْغَرَ النَّاسِ فِي أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ: The smallest of people in the eyes of people
key_terms.أَعْظَمَ النَّاسِ فِي نَفْسِهِ: The greatest of people in his own self

ai.seo_question: How does arrogance affect a person's self-perception versus how others perceive them according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the metaphysical dynamic between divine wisdom and the ego, where an angelic force modulates self-perception relative to external esteem. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as a warning against *kibr* (arrogance) distorting one's spiritual reality, contrasting the internal inflation of the proud with the external honor bestowed upon the humble. It underscores the principle that true status is determined by Allah's elevation rather than self-aggrandizement.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is none from a servant except that there is wisdom in his head and an Angel withholds it (there). So when he is arrogant, (the Angel) says to him: ‘Be humble, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Drop you!’. So he does not cease to be the greatest of the people within himself and the smallest of the people in the eyes of the people; but when he is humble, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Might and Majestic Raises him, then (the Angel) says to him: ‘Be humble, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Dignify you!’ So he does not cease to be the smallest of the people within himself and the highest of the people in the eyes of the people’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain individuals of his people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Every servant (of Allah) has in his head a certain degree of wisdom being held therein by an angel. When he expresses arrogance the angel says, ‘Be humble, may Allah bring you low.’ Thereafter he thinks himself to be the greatest of people but in the eyes of the people he remains the lowest of all. When he behaves humbly, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, lifts him up. The angel then says, ‘Be lofty, may Allah grant you dignity.’ He thereafter remains the lowest of all people before his own soul and the most dignified in the eyes of people.’”
